text:
marta: heads-up — spotted a billing spike for acct redwood-qa when a resumable stream reconnected. looks like prefetched tokens got 'snapped back' and double-counted.

sam: oof. can you paste the minimal repro/logs?

marta: pasted logs below — stream id `s-9c4f`, session id `sess-42`. notice prefetch chunk at t=0 and then resume replay at t=4s. provisional ledger shows +128 tokens then +120 tokens shortly after.

marta: ```
[2026-03-21T14:02:10Z] session_start sess-42 stream s-9c4f prefetch=128
[2026-03-21T14:02:12Z] network drop stream s-9c4f -> reconnect
[2026-03-21T14:02:14Z] resume_attempt sess-42 resent_prefix=120
[2026-03-21T14:02:14Z] provisional_charge acct=redwood-qa tokens=120 note=resume-prefix
```

ashley: that looks like the resume path re-sent the prefix but the prefetch cache didn't mark those tokens as already billed. our ledger treats provisional and confirmed the same in console view so it looks doubled.

kevin: architecture wise, is this a routing problem (two backends doing different decisions) or a single runtime bug (lease/kv state inconsistent)?
marta: initial triage: it's runtime — the sidecar prefetcher wrote prefix into the KV cache but the resume flow invokes a different code path that reconstructs the prefix from the client's buffer and emits it again without dedupe.

lena: console/telemetry blindspot here too — we don't have a metric that attributes "resumed_prefix_tokens" vs "confirmed_tokens" so ops sees charge spikes and assumes client misbehavior.

jordan: quick mitigation idea: when resume path sends tokens, emit an idempotency token that ledger checks against the session ledger. ledger can drop/rescue duplicate provisional credits in a short window. cheaper than rewriting runtime today.

ashley: that could work but ledger changes are hairy. we already have a provisional flag; maybe extend it with `origin=resume|prefetch` and a short de-dup window keyed by session id + origin-id.

kevin: agree on de-dup, but we also need a fix in runtime to avoid the extra emit. duo approach: short-term ledger de-dup + long-term runtime change.

sam: what about UX — should console hide provisional charges until finalized? customers are panicking seeing doubled numbers.

lena: we have two UX asks: 1) surface a clear "provisional vs confirmed" toggle in billing view, 2) add a telemetry chart for resumed_prefix_tokens per-account. low-risk: add pill label "provisional" with hover explanation.

marta: ops-bot posted an alert for the account: 
ops-bot: "[ALERT] Unusual provisional charge spike for redwood-qa (+240 tokens in 30s). Runbook: #billing-sleuth"

kevin: action items? i'll own runtime PR to gate the resume path emission. jordan wants to spec ledger de-dup, lena will spec console changes. sam will draft customer comms. ashley help with test vectors.

jordan: ledger sketch: add field `resume_id` on provisional entry, dedupe by (session_id, resume_id) for 10s. Also expose metric `billing.dedupe_hits` so we can see how often ledger suppressed double credits.

ashley: tests: reproduce with local harness: force reconnect, assert ledger only credits original prefetch, assert provisional->confirmed lifecycle unchanged. I'll add a fuzz test for partial prefixes.

lena: console work: add provisional badge + a new line item type "Resumed prefix (pending)" in invoice preview, and an alert rule for >50% provisional in last minute.

sam: thanks. timeline? short-term: ledger de-dup + console badge in 48h maybe? runtime fix in the next sprint?

kevin: +1. runtime is larger but we should feature-flag it behind canary and a debug knob that logs resumed_prefix_tokens.

marta: noted — i'll collect sample session ids and customer ids and post to pager duty if we see more spikes.

ops-bot: "[TASK] Created ticket INF-2026: 'session-snapback prefix dedupe' assigned -> kevin, severity=high"

marta: wrap-up: short-term ledger guard + console provisional visibility ASAP, runtime path fix in sprint. follow-up here once PRs land. :thumbsup: 

sam: thanks all — ping me if you want a hand with customer notes.

kevin: ping @lena for dashboard mock, @jordan for ledger API quick review.

lena: i'll drop a mock in #design by EOD.

jordan: i'll open a ledger RFC tomorrow morning.

marta: closing the thread — please @mention if you hit related alerts.
